To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ecosystem water use efficiency of cropland can be directly and effectively quantified using the enhanced vegetation index derived from MODIS satellite data.
MODIS EVI is a good proxy for the ecosystem water use efficiency of croplands and that the empirical model based on MODIS-EVI can be used to estimate WUE at regional scales.

(1) MODIS EVI is a good proxy for ecosystem water use efficiency of cropland; (2) MODIS EVIs are strongly correlated with ecosystem water use efficiency, and the relationship is mainly driven by solar radiation and temperature; (3) the simple model that is solely built upon MODIS EVI can capture the temporal variations in ecosystem water use efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and accurate method for monitoring WUE of croplands by exclusive use of remote-sensing data.
the direct estimation of ecosystem WUE by exclusive use of remote sensing data.
the development of an efficient approach to estimate ecosystem WUE of croplands by exclusive use of the MODIS EVI time-series data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MODIS EVI time-series are a useful and promising tool for the direct and accurate estimation of WUE at regional scale.
the direct MODIS EVI-based approach can be used for large scale monitoring of WUE of corn and soybean croplands.

the MODIS-based method has the potential to provide reliable estimates of WUE, and the method could be further improved through integration of more remote sensing products, such as leaf area index, and ground measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MODIS-derived WUe can be estimated by the exclusive use of EVI data and is a promising tool for large-area monitoring.
the direct estimation by exclusive use of remote sensing data is more reliable for quantifying the temporal variations of WUE than the indirect estimation by combining remote sensing products.
MODIS EVI can be directly used to estimate ecosystem WUE, and the empirical model can be used to estimate WUE at the regional scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MODIS EVI can serve as an effective proxy of ecosystem WUE and can potentially be used for regional-scale monitoring of WUE.
WUE can be estimated by exclusive use of EVI data, and this method is particularly useful for regions with a lack of eddy covariance observations and limited access to other remotely sensed data.
MODIS-derived EVI data can be directly used to track the temporal variations in ecosystem WUE, and the method can be applied to other ecosystems.
